_note: What an answer has to contain, as facts rather than as a sentence. Instructions for whoever writes the line and never shown to a player, so like voices.json this file is English only and is not translated: a translated copy of a brief is two things to keep in step for no benefit. Keyed npc.intent. An option that is not in here is never generated and its hand-written reply stands, which is what makes turning generation on safe one line at a time.
_why_note: The packet used to end with MUST SAY followed by the whole finished reply, which is a brief to rephrase rather than a brief to write. Rephrasing is safe and nearly worthless: if the sentence is already written, generating it again buys nothing. Facts are the brief that earns its keep, because 71 fact sets cover the thousands of situations the 71 hand-written replies cannot tell apart.
_context_note: Every fact carries why, not just what. 'the works has killed 381 men' leaves a player asking 381 of what and why does that matter; 'and Arthur reads the number every spring and orders the works made bigger' is the half that makes the first half mean something. A line can only be self-contained if the brief was.

halgrave.ask_works: the works makes iron and steel: rails, plates, tools, nails
before the works, 1 child in 4 born here died every winter; now it is 1 in 40
he believes the works is why the town is alive at all
halgrave.ask_cost: the works has killed 381 men in 11 years
he writes the number down himself and sends it to King Arthur every spring
Arthur reads it and orders the works made bigger, every year
halgrave.ask_ledger: he keeps a book with every dead man's name and the date he died
the crown asks him for the book each year, and he would keep it anyway
his reason: if a thing kills 381 men, somebody should write it down

the tradesman went to prison for 4 months
the poor one went to prison for 7 years
same wall, same night, same law
